shouldFix.title: The CLAUDE-DAJ4-A2 repair carves PT-FS-WRITE-HOST-STATE out of the component tail as an unqualified token-level typing claim, under D-032 extraction standing that adopted D-032 does not supply at that scope, contradicting both the artifact's own broad tail rule in the same sentence and the DR-105 component scoping in both recorded permission generations
evidence: componentTails opens with the load-bearing broad rule: 'After a host CA-1 SPAWN decision has produced an admitted component child, EVERY subsequent effect of that admitted child stays in DR-105.' Three sentences later, in the same clause, it states without qualification: 'PT-FS-WRITE-HOST-STATE is host operational-metadata / BLK-6, not a component tail.' That is a token-level exclusion, not an actor-scoped one; it is stated of the token, not of a particular writer.

The same unqualified exclusion is carried into the fixture class at /joinFixtureClasses/classes/3: '...PT-FS-WRITE-HOST-STATE is host operational-metadata / BLK-6, not a component tail...'. Fixture classes are what DR-G09 authors against, so the exclusion is the form that would be executed.

/extractedDecidedClauses/standing binds the scope of that claim: 'EXTRACTED from adopted D-032 unless a clause names a different source. Clauses marked NAMED from recorded host-effect are environment from the D-093/D-126 candidates, not D-032 extraction.' componentTails names no different source and carries no NAMED marking, so the exclusion asserts D-032 extraction standing.

Adopted D-032 does not supply it at that scope. COORD lines 1646-1649, carried verbatim in this subject at /d032DecidedActorSplitCarriedVerbatim, read: 'BLK-6 DISCHARGED-AS-INAPPLICABLE for host / default **reads and** doctor's operational-metadata write / (FS-WRITE-HOST-STATE is not a component grant; fail-closed if that / class is denied)'. The parenthetical at line 1648 attaches to 'doctor's operational-metadata write' at line 1647. Its subject is the doctor/host actor's own write, and the clause it qualifies is a BLK-6 discharge about that actor.

The artifact itself states the correct actor-scoped form elsewhere. /extractedDecidedClauses/hostDefaultReadsAndOperationalMetadataWrite reads: 'EXTRACTED from D-032 BLK-6 DISCHARGED-AS-INAPPLICABLE: host default reads and doctor's operational-metadata write (FS-WRITE-HOST-STATE is not a component grant).' That clause keeps the actor ('doctor's'). componentTails and FC-JOIN-COMPONENT-TAIL drop it. The artifact therefore holds the actor-scoped form and the token-level form simultaneously; they are not the same claim, and the broad one is not the one D-032 supports.

Both recorded permission generations contradict the token-level form, and their text is byte-identical across the two generations, which I re-verified in each file rather than taking from either. permission-truth-tables.v2 (D-042, the accepted DR-105 candidate, pinned at /recordedInputs) and permission-truth-tables.v6 (D-109) both carry: {'token': 'PT-FS-WRITE-HOST-STATE', 'effectClass': 'filesystem/state', 'meaning': 'Create, modify, or remove bytes inside the host-owned state namespace allocated to this component for its declared state class.'}. The scopeParameter is 'The declared state class plus the host-allocated namespace path for this component.' The sliceJustification states the token 'is the local write half of D-002's DR-105 scoping.'

The token is component-requested in both generations: v6 records at its REQUESTED row for PT-FS-WRITE-HOST-STATE that 'The admitted manifest's permissions[] block names this token with a reason.' A manifest permissions[] block is a component surface, not a doctor-side one.

Consequence at the actor boundary. An admitted CA-1 SPAWN child that writes into the host-owned state namespace allocated to it is, by the artifact's own broad rule, a subsequent effect of the admitted child and stays in DR-105. By the excluding sentence it is instead host operational-metadata under BLK-6 — a class D-032 marks DISCHARGED-AS-INAPPLICABLE. That routes a component effect out of DR-105's component-grant requirement. It is the mirror image of the leak the artifact does name at /extractedDecidedClauses/inheritedPermissionRecitalConflict, where a CA-1/CA-2 recital is called out for putting host acts onto an admitted-component PT-NET-EGRESS tail; here an admitted-component act is taken off the component tail and put onto a host discharge.

Both readings of the source are defective, so the finding does not depend on my reading winning. If D-032's parenthetical is actor-scoped, as its line placement indicates, the exclusion is an over-extraction carrying false D-032 extraction standing — the same defect class the artifact repaired for the D-000 CA-2 gate at CLAUDE-DAJ4-A1 and invites attack on at /reviewGuidance ('Attack attributing the later D-000 CA-2 gate to D-032 extraction'). If instead the parenthetical is token-level, it collides head-on with the DR-105 scoping in recorded permission v2 and v6, and the artifact resolves that collision silently in D-032's favour while explicitly declining to resolve the adjacent PT-NET-EGRESS recital conflict, which it names as inherited and unresolved. The artifact cannot be right on both clauses at once.
shouldFix.whyNotAdvisory: It is not confined to wording. The exclusion is asserted twice, once in the extracted clause that governs the tail and once in the fixture class DR-G09 would author against, and it changes which register a class of admitted-child effect lands in. The frozen v4 lane rated the adjacent point ADVISORY when it concerned only which representative routes to name; this concerns re-typing a route that both recorded permission generations scope to DR-105.
shouldFix.whyNotBlocker: The artifact binds NOTHING, applies nothing, authors and executes no fixtures, and this defect mints no grant, admits no unexercisable act, SATISFIES nothing and authorizes no implementation. It is calibrated to the frozen precedent: CLAUDE-DAJ4-S1, an actor-boundary mis-typing of comparable reach, was rated SHOULD-FIX.
shouldFix.repairDirection: Not authored here. Either restore the actor scope the source carries — the doctor/host actor's own operational-metadata write under that class is BLK-6 and not a component tail, while an admitted child's own PT-FS-WRITE-HOST-STATE write into its allocated namespace stays in DR-105 under the broad rule — or, if the token-level reading is intended, name it as an inherited conflict with recorded permission v2/v6 DR-105 scoping alongside the PT-NET-EGRESS recital rather than resolving it silently.

advisories.title: CLAUDE-DAJ4-A2 is recorded as REPAIRED, but the recorded repair departs from what the frozen advisory asked for rather than satisfying it
advisories.observation: The frozen v4 Claude advisory named six non-egress component routes as 'available and stable in both permission generations, which I re-verified rather than took: PT-FS-READ-PROJECT, PT-FS-READ-COMPONENT, PT-FS-WRITE-HOST-STATE, PT-PROC-EXEC-DECLARED, PT-ENV-READ, PT-HOST-EFFECT-BROKERED', and asked only that 'naming two or three would match the roster's own style without authoring fixtures.' v5 names four of the six and affirmatively re-types a fifth, PT-FS-WRITE-HOST-STATE, out of the component tail. The disposition line records that as 'REPAIRED' at 'FC-JOIN-COMPONENT-TAIL names PT-FS-READ-PROJECT, PT-FS-READ-COMPONENT, PT-PROC-EXEC-DECLARED, PT-ENV-READ; excludes PT-FS-WRITE-HOST-STATE'. Excluding a route the advisory listed as a component route is a substantive departure from the advisory, not a discharge of it, and the accounting record does not say so. This is the accounting half of CLAUDE-DAJ5-S1 and is raised separately because it concerns the disposition record rather than the typing claim; repairing S1 should also correct how this disposition is described.
advisories.notAFinding: The silent omission of PT-HOST-EFFECT-BROKERED is not charged. componentTails and FC-JOIN-COMPONENT-TAIL both hedge the list as 'representative', so naming a subset is within what the advisory asked for.

verdictBasis: The dispatch permits ACCEPT only at zero blockers and zero SHOULD-FIX. This review returns zero blockers and one SHOULD-FIX, so the verdict is REJECT. Custody, the closed roster, the carried D-032 block, the register row, all twenty recorded inputs and all eight frozen predecessor verdicts reproduce with zero mismatches, and I could not break the artifact on any of the attacks its own reviewGuidance invites, including the five-member roster coverage attack. Three of the four claimed repairs — CLAUDE-DAJ4-S1, CLAUDE-DAJ4-A1 and DAJ4-CX-A1 — are genuine and I verified each against its cited source rather than its repair note; the CLAUDE-DAJ4-S1 repair in particular is well made and correctly attributed. The fourth introduced the defect: repairing the ADVISORY about which component routes to name, the artifact excluded one of them by asserting a token-level typing claim that adopted D-032 supports only of the doctor/host actor, that both recorded permission generations scope to DR-105 and to the component, and that contradicts the artifact's own broad tail rule in the same sentence. The artifact states the correct actor-scoped form in a neighbouring clause, which is why this reads as an over-extraction rather than a decision.
